questiontext.text:
{@E[1]@}

Type \(\le\) as <= and \(\ge\) as >=, for example 4x+9y<=72. Use the letters x and y as defined in the question.

(a) Write the inequality that makes sure there is enough.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the whole-number plan with the least waste. \(x =\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] \(y =\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

(c) How many {@un@} are wasted with your plan? [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) \({@ta1@}\), with \({@uc@}x + {@ud@}y \le {@RR@}\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

(b) The waste is \(W = {@ga@}x + {@gb@}y - {@NN@}\). Test the whole-number plans of R near the line \({@ga@}x + {@gb@}y = {@NN@}\): the least waste is at \(x = {@bst[1]@}\), \(y = {@bst[2]@}\).

(c) \({@ga@} \times {@bst[1]@} + {@gb@} \times {@bst[2]@} - {@NN@} = {@W@}\) {@un@}. Making the most of what you have is the same as making the least waste.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: least waste

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (d, e) / Essential 1.4 (d, e): Write an at-least requirement, then find the whole-number plan within a limit that leaves the least waste, and the amount wasted.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: k1: lcls(ans1, ta1); w1: lcls(ans1, sw1);

truefeedback.text: Your inequality says the total is \({@NN@}\) {@un@} or less. ‘At least \({@NN@}\)’ means the total cannot go below \({@NN@}\).
You matched the amounts to the wrong letters: each of the \(x\) items gives \({@ga@}\) {@un@}.

falsefeedback.text: Total = (amount from one) \(\times\, x\) + (amount from the other) \(\times\, y\), and it must be at least \({@NN@}\).

feedbackvariables.text: enough: is(ga*ans2 + gb*ans3 >= NN); lim: is(uc*ans2 + ud*ans3 <= RR and ans2 >= 0 and ans3 >= 0);

falsefeedback.text: Your plan needs \({@uc*ans2+ud*ans3@}\), more than the \({@RR@}\) available.

truefeedback.text: That plan uses the fewest items but leaves \({@Wfew@}\) {@un@} over; another plan leaves less.

falsefeedback.text: Your plan leaves \({@Wof(ans2, ans3)@}\) {@un@} over. Try other plans near the line \({@ga@}x + {@gb@}y = {@NN@}\).

truefeedback.text: That is right for your plan in (b), but your plan is not the one with the least waste.
That is the total made. The waste is the total minus \({@NN@}\).

falsefeedback.text: Your plan in (b) makes \({@ga@} \times {@ans2@} + {@gb@} \times {@ans3@}\) {@un@}. The waste is what is left over after the \({@NN@}\) needed.
